The population standard deviation is not known. A sample of 24 batteries has a mean battery life of 9.33 hours. The sample standard deviation is 1.35 hours. Use a one-sample t test at the 0.05 significance level. Test the claim that the true mean battery life is less than 10 hours. State the null and alternative hypotheses. Then write a conclusion in context.

intermediate.problemText: A testing lab studies the battery life of a particular battery model. Each observation is the battery life, in hours, of one fully charged battery. The manufacturer’s claim is that the population mean battery life is 10 hours. In a random sample of 24 batteries, the sample mean battery life is 9.33 hours and the sample standard deviation is 1.35 hours. At the 0.05 significance level, is there enough evidence to support the claim that the true mean battery life for this model is less than 10 hours? State the null and alternative hypotheses, show your work, calculate the P-value, and write a conclusion in context.
linguisticNotes: Uses standard introductory statistics wording such as “population mean,” “sample mean,” “sample standard deviation,” and “significance level.”
Avoids Greek-letter notation and symbolic hypotheses.
Does not explicitly name the t test; the sample standard deviation is provided so the method is inferred.
Maintains the left-tailed alternative by asking whether the true mean is less than 10 hours.

Formulate the null and alternative claims, report the P-value, and draw a contextual conclusion for the product-testing setting.

Researchers are testing the true average clotting time. This is the population mean. The null claim says the mean is 5 minutes. The alternative claim says the mean is different from 5 minutes.

The population standard deviation is not known. A sample has 52 blood samples. The sample mean is 5.38 minutes. The sample standard deviation is 1 minute. Use the 0.025 significance level.

Perform the appropriate one-sample t test. State the null and alternative hypotheses. Then write a conclusion in context.

States the null claim and two-tailed alternative claim clearly in words.
Lists the sample size, sample mean, sample standard deviation, and significance level in separate sentences.

At the 0.025 significance level, is there enough evidence to support the claim that the population mean clotting time is different from 5 minutes? State the null and alternative hypotheses in words, show your work, calculate the p-value, make a decision, and write a conclusion in context.
